etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin alternō (“take turns”), from alternus (“one after another, by turns”), from alter (“other”) + -rnus. See altern, alter.

definitions.definition: (heraldry) Alternating; (of e.g. a pair of tinctures which a charge is coloured) succeeding in turns, or (relative to the field) counterchanged.

quote.citation: 1925, The Jewish Encyclopedia: Chazars-Dreyfus Case, page 128:
quote.text: Goldschmidt (Austria; creation July 27, 1862): [...] party, argent and gules, an eagle of alternate colors, [...]

definitions.definition: Happening by turns; one following the other in succession of time or place; first one and then the other (repeatedly).

quote.citation: 1711 May, [Alexander Pope], An Essay on Criticism, London:  […]  W[illiam] Lewis […]; and sold by W[illiam] Taylor […], T[homas] Osborn[e] […], and J[ohn] Graves […], →OCLC:
quote.text: And bid alternate passions fall and rise

quote.citation: 1960 September, “Talking of Trains: Newcastle signal area enlarged”, in Trains Illustrated, page 522:
quote.text: One of the two boxes displaced by the new Pelaw installation will be Springwell, between Boldon Colliery and Pelaw, which has recently had the distinction of being manned by a husband and wife on alternate shifts.

quote.citation: 2021 December 15, Robin Leleux, “Awards honour the best restoration projects: The Arch Company Award for Urban Heritage: Knaresborough”, in RAIL, number 946, page 56:
quote.text: The service is half-hourly as far as Harrogate and Knaresborough, with alternate trains going on to York.

definitions.definition: (mathematics) Designating the members in a series, which regularly intervene between the members of another series, as the odd or even numbers of the numerals; every other; every second.
(botany, of leaves) Distributed singly at different heights of the stem, and at equal intervals as respects angular divergence[1]
That which alternates with something else; vicissitude.

quote.citation: 1718, Mat[thew] Prior, “Solomon on the Vanity of the World. A Poem in Three Books.”, in Poems on Several Occasions, London:  […]  Jacob Tonson […], and John Barber […], →OCLC, (please specify the page):

definitions.definition: (US) A substitute; an alternative; one designated to take the place of another, if necessary, in performing some duty.

quote.citation: 2007 September 25, Bungie, Halo 3, spoken by Cortana (Jen Taylor), Microsoft Game Studios, Xbox 360, level/area: Cortana:
quote.text: Corridors beyond this point have collapsed. I'm looking for an alternate. Careful.

definitions.definition: (mathematics) A proportion derived from another proportion by interchanging the means.
(US) A replacement of equal or greater value or function.
(transitive) To perform by turns, or in succession; to cause to succeed by turns; to interchange regularly.

quote.text: The most high God, in all things appertaining unto this life, for sundry wise ends alternates the disposition of good and evil.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To happen, succeed, or act by turns; to follow reciprocally in place or time; followed by with.
(transitive, geometry) To perform an alternation (removal of alternate vertices) on (a polytope or tessellation); to remove vertices (from a face or edge) as part of an alternation.

quote.citation: 1932, Harold Scott Macdonald Coxeter, The densities of the regular polytopes, part 2‎[1], reprinted in 1995, F. Arthur Sherk, Peter Mcmullen, Anthony C. Thompson, Asia Ivić Weiss (editors), Kaleidoscopes: Selected Writings of H. S. M. Coxeter, page 54:
quote.text: This case suggests that the alternation of a polyhedron should be bounded by actual vertex figures and alternated faces. The case of the cube is in agreement with this notion, since the alternated square is nothing.
